observations.got: The top-left patch contains rendered imagery at about 16x16 pixels; the user reports it changing. The 110s screenshot shows incomplete dark geometry, figures and fire at 3 FPS / 334.4 ms. The FPS overlay is at the upper right. The captures do not establish that all missing graphics are compressed into the patch.
observations.gow: GPU is busy at 100% during the late stall; driver reports insufficient memory for submission followed by ErrorDeviceLost. Whole-device VRAM use is about 10.7GB at 107s out of 25.75GB. Device memory exhaustion is not established. Root kernel captures contain only 600 repeated errors around the end and cannot establish the first cause.
observations.performance: GoT: 916208 draw calls, 322393 dispatch calls, 21.72s inclusive GPU waits and 11.20s self texture binding across the run. GoW live snapshot at about 117s: 4.35 million page-protect calls / 12.82s, 41.72s inclusive GPU waits and 31.75s inclusive ordered-DS work (nested costs, not additive). These are host region costs, not per-frame GPU timing.

changes: Compute mip/layer offsets from the final backing rather than the last examined overlap; preserve the requested relative view and undo prior backing offsets during rebinding.
Use one-layer byte stride to calculate a subarray base layer; reject underflow, zero strides and ranges extending beyond the mip.
Copy valid GPU contents before retiring an overlapping bound target/texture, mark required rebinds, and keep fresh backing contents when the old image is CPU dirty.
Bounded unique small-render-pass logs expose addresses, dimensions, view, viewport, scissor and pipeline stages; sparse subresource mapping events show resolved views.

GPU work ring grows from 2048 to 16384 entries with an 8MiB output cap. Kernel collection uses the native start time and preserves both beginning and end up to 8MiB, with truncation metadata. Console retention grows to 64MiB.
Original OpenOrbis subarray probe supplied under tools/hardware/subresource-alias; two paired cases compare relative array-layer aliasing.

validation.fixture_scope: Production FindImage, ResolveOverlap, MipOf and SliceOf are extracted unchanged; Vulkan operations and backing storage are substituted. These are host checks, not native rendering validation.
validation.native_build: PASS GCC14 Release full link after explicit reconfigure at pinned source
validation.retained_cpu_suite: PASS: 31 CTests; renderer, SRT, sparse arena, descriptors, contiguous VMA, unexpected Vulkan error and guest/HLE ABI checks
validation.hardware_probe: Strict host C11 syntax passes; SDK linking and physical GPU execution not performed. Probe covers relative array views, not mip-chain overlap order. No new guest ISA/kernel behavior is implemented by the host cache correction.
validation.runner: PASS interval arguments, noninteractive sudo-only collection, head/tail retention, truncation flags, Bash/Python syntax, observer/runner/wrapper checksums

open_issues: Native corner cause and full scene lighting/geometry remain unverified.
GoW cutscene GPU loss and low FPS remain unresolved; earliest kernel failure was absent in the supplied tail.
Three runtime sample-offset warnings in GoT still represent an unimplemented path. No offsets are fabricated by this patch.
Unflattened SHARP warnings (GoT 609, GoW 224) require descriptor provenance/capture; warnings alone do not prove the runtime fallback failed.
GoT scaled min/max blend warnings remain; format=0 in this log is the numeric format value, not proof an attachment is absent.
Descriptor pool growth messages are handled by the existing allocator; the new capture has no descriptor-allocation crash.
Layer-count coercion messages and active depth/stencil readback limitations remain under review.
Missing dumped fonts/trophy resources and GoW wypsm file-open failures are recorded; optional versus required file status is unverified. No guest files are fabricated.
Unimplemented service stubs, compute queue register 0xb, wave-limit hints and Oodle usage warnings are audited but not claimed implemented or causal.
